verdict.rationale: Godot ships a genuinely documented scriptable interface for editor automation: EditorScript/_run() for in-editor scripting, EditorInterface for controlling the editor window, saving/loading scenes, and editing resources/objects, an editor plugin system usable without reloading, and a CLI/headless mode that supports scripted builds and exports (godot-docs-5, godot-docs-20, godot-docs-22, godot-docs-3, godot-docs-19, godot-probe-4). This collectively lets a script (which an AI agent could generate and invoke) create scenes/nodes, edit properties, and trigger exports/builds programmatically. However, this is a general-purpose scripting/automation API rather than an AI-agent-native interface — there is no official MCP server or agent-specific protocol (godot-probe-rt-3, godot-probe-rt-4), and no hands-on evidence of an AI agent successfully driving the editor this way. Missing for 10: an official agent-facing protocol (MCP or similar), independent/hands-on confirmation that an AI agent can reliably use EditorScript/EditorInterface/CLI end-to-end.
